This allows the memory to be freed and potentially overwritten by another thread, leading to undefined behavior and potential exposure of sensitive information.

vul_knowledge.solution_behavior: To mitigate the vulnerability, it is necessary to duplicate the 'Content-Type' string into a new memory location managed by the Apache request pool before setting the header. This ensures that the memory remains valid for the duration of the request, preventing any potential issues related to premature memory freeing. In this case, the solution involves modifying the code to use apr_pstrdup(r->pool, value) when setting the 'Content-Type' header.
